title: Late-Rush Refund on an Appraisal Order
content:
**Appraisal Order — late-rush refund.** When a borrower has paid for rush turn time and the report is late against its due date (the date the completed report is promised), a late-rush refund returns part or all of the rush charge. The late-rush refund names the rush charge entry it returns and goes back to the card or account that rush charge was collected with. It is recorded on the order's rush line with the refund reason that the rush promise was missed.

### Issuing the refund

This is an agent-side action. The agent unlocks `refund_late_rush_charge_6e5bda3a` and then calls it; each call books one refund, dated today, against one rush charge entry.

| Parameter | Meaning | Format and values |
|---|---|---|
| `appraisal_order_id` | Reference number of the Appraisal Order the rush charge was collected on, as returned by the appraisal order lookup | Identifier |
| `original_fee_entry_id` | Reference number of the rush charge entry being returned, as returned by the appraisal fee history lookup for the order | Identifier |
| `refund_amount` | Amount returned to the borrower, in US dollars | Positive number, 2 decimal places; stored rounded to 2 decimal places |
| `payment_method` | The card or account the refund is returned to | `debit_card` when the rush charge was collected from the borrower's debit card; `credit_card` when it was collected from the borrower's credit card; `ach_debit` when it was debited from the borrower's bank account by ACH |

**Successful return.** A record with `appraisal_fee_entry_id` (reference number of the new refund entry), `original_fee_entry_id` (the rush charge entry returned), `fee_component` (always `rush_fee`), `amount` (the amount refunded, US dollars, 2 decimal places), `refund_reason` (always `rush_deadline_missed`), `entry_date` (today, year-month-day), `fee_balance` (the order's net appraisal charges paid after the refund, US dollars, 2 decimal places) and `status` (always `refunded`). A status of refunded means the refund now stands on the order: the order's fee history has gained one refund entry on the rush line naming the charge entry it returns, and the order's net appraisal charges paid have fallen by exactly the refunded amount; the borrower sees the refund on the card or account it is returned to.

*Hypothetical illustration:* returning 75.00 of a 150.00 rush charge collected by `debit_card` books one refund entry of 75.00 on the rush line naming that charge entry, with `fee_balance` 75.00 lower than before.
